title: Ankhorage Cognito Auth
summary: Implements the provider-neutral Ankhorage authentication port with Amazon Cognito User Pools.
purpose: Provide a standalone Cognito authentication adapter with explicit host-owned session and authorization-attempt persistence.
responsibilities: Implement password, session, refresh, sign-out, password-reset, and brokered OAuth flows through Cognito User Pools.
Verify Cognito access and identity JWTs before accepting provider identities or sessions.
Translate Cognito and AWS failures into provider-neutral authentication results.
boundaries: Does not own application user profiles or authorization policy.
Does not persist sessions or authorization attempts; the host supplies those stores.
Does not expose AWS credentials through its public configuration.
audience: Applications that use Amazon Cognito User Pools behind the Ankhorage authentication port.
Hosts that provide secure session and one-time authorization-attempt persistence.
useCases: Authenticate and register users with Cognito password flows.
Complete a PKCE authorization flow through a configured Cognito identity provider.
Read, refresh, and revoke a host-persisted Cognito session.

architecture.role: Provider adapter at the Amazon Cognito boundary for the published AuthPort.
invariants: Stable Cognito subject identifiers are derived from verified JWT claims.
Session and authorization-attempt state remains host-owned and authorization attempts are consumed once.
Provider failures are normalized without exposing provider payloads or secrets.

configuration: Requires a Cognito region, User Pool identifier, app-client identifier, hosted domain, and explicit redirect URI allowlist.
Requires host-provided session and authorization-attempt stores and an AWS Cognito client.
security: Cognito JWT signature, issuer, client, token-use, expiry, subject, and OAuth nonce bindings are verified before a session is trusted.
Authorization uses PKCE and one-time state stored outside the adapter.
limitations: OTP verification is not represented as a signed Cognito session by the generic AuthPort.
